meta.topic: Statistician vs Data Scientist (vs Growth Engineer / AI Engineer) — labor & practice stats for interactive industry-vertical comparison

reference_periods.bls_ooh_edition: OOH 2025 edition, page last-modified 2026-08-27, using May-2025 OEWS wage data and 2025-2035 employment projections
reference_periods.bls_oews_news_release: USDL-26-0725, released 2026-05-15, 'May 2025' reference period (Table 1, national A01 results)

caveats: BLS OOH employment figures and OEWS news-release employment figures differ slightly for the same occupation-year because they come from two related but separately-modeled BLS data products (OOH uses the Employment Projections program; the news release table is the raw OEWS survey estimate). Both are cited below, labeled by source.
Job-posting counts are live snapshots taken 2026-09-14 and will drift within hours; Indeed in particular shows rounded/bucketed counts in its page title, not exact live totals.

'Growth engineer' and 'AI engineer' have no official BLS SOC occupation code — no OOH/OEWS entry exists for either. All labor stats for them are proxied via adjacent SOC codes or sourced from job boards / industry surveys only.

growth_engineer.bls_status: No official BLS SOC occupation code and no OOH/OEWS entry exists. For visa/immigration SOC-mapping purposes, practitioners map 'growth engineer' ad hoc to Software Developers (15-1252) or Marketing Manager depending on duty split.
growth_engineer.definition: A software engineer embedded within a Growth or Marketing team whose mission is to build technical systems that accelerate acquisition, activation, retention and revenue: A/B testing infrastructure, funnel/cohort instrumentation, feature-flag systems, lifecycle triggers, attribution, landing/signup/checkout flows.

ai_engineer.bls_status: No dedicated BLS SOC occupation code. Duties are typically absorbed into Computer and Information Research Scientists (15-1221), Data Scientists (15-2051), or Software Developers (15-1252) depending on the role's ML/research vs production-engineering balance.
ai_engineer.market_signal_note: See job_postings.wellfound and job_postings.indeed — AI engineer posting volume is the highest of the four roles studied on every board checked.

computer_and_information_research_scient.growth_context: BLS attributes growth to AI development, data-mining services, and cybersecurity demand.

kaggle_state_of_data_science.status: Kaggle has not published an official 'State of Data Science and Machine Learning' report since 2022. A community-uploaded raw dataset labeled '2025 Kaggle Machine Learning and Data Science Survey' exists on Kaggle but is not an official Kaggle-authored report.

tool_usage_pct_secondary_source.source: Towards Data Science, 'Data Science Trends Based on 4 Years of Kaggle Surveys'

burtch_works_2025_ai_data_science_compen.ai_vs_ds_premium_pct: 9-13% cash premium for AI professionals over Data Scientists at comparable levels, widest where scarce Gen-AI expertise adds most value
burtch_works_2025_ai_data_science_compen.yoy_note: Data Science saw statistically significant base-pay gains at IC-1/2 and MG-1/2; AI compensation showed no changes exceeding the 5% significance threshold.

oreilly_2025_technology_trends.note: This is a platform-usage trends report, not a compensation survey. O'Reilly's dedicated 'Data/AI Salary Survey' series appears discontinued after its 2021 edition (avg salary $146,000; modal band $100k-$150k, 34% of respondents).

levels_fyi.caveat: Levels.fyi's sample skews toward large, stock-granting tech employers (Google, Meta, Microsoft, Atlassian all show $250K-$315K medians) and is not representative of the full labor market the way BLS OEWS is.

pwc_2025_global_ai_jobs_barometer.sample_basis: ~1 billion job ads across six continents
pwc_2025_global_ai_jobs_barometer.skills_change_velocity: Skills required in AI-exposed jobs changing 66% faster than less-exposed jobs
pwc_2025_global_ai_jobs_barometer.fetch_note: Direct WebFetch to pwc.com returned HTTP 403 twice; figures corroborated across four independent pwc.com regional subdomains (gx, us, id, hk) returned by search, so confidence remains high despite not reading the primary PDF directly.

practice_differences.statistician: Inference: designing studies, quantifying uncertainty, choosing estimators, defending a result under scrutiny.
practice_differences.data_scientist: Prediction: building and deploying predictive/ML models optimized for forecast accuracy.

practice_differences.statistician: Hypothesis-driven, scientific approach; tests specific pre-registered hypotheses.
Models built to accurately describe the relationship between variables (explanatory).
practice_differences.data_scientist: Models built to predict outcomes (predictive), typically shipped into production.

practice_differences.statistician: Usually provided with tidy, already-curated data.
practice_differences.data_scientist: Spends significant time gathering and cleaning imperfect, messy raw data.

practice_differences.statistician: SPSS, SAS, Minitab, MATLAB, design-of-experiments methods.
practice_differences.data_scientist: TensorFlow, Spark, Docker, Kubernetes, cloud ML platforms (SageMaker, Azure ML, GCP), Airflow.

practice_differences.statistician: 62% hold a master's degree as highest credential (O*NET).
practice_differences.data_scientist: 48% bachelor's / 44% master's split — a materially lower graduate-degree bar (O*NET).

practice_differences.statistician: Concentrated in federal government (16%), scientific R&D (15%), healthcare (8%) — regulated/scientific institutions.
practice_differences.data_scientist: Concentrated in publishing/media (12%), insurance (10%), computer systems design (10%), corporate management (10%) — commercial/tech-adjacent institutions.
practice_differences.source: BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook, Work Environment sections (see roles.statistician / roles.data_scientist above)

practice_differences.statistician_and_data_scientist: Both hold a formal BLS SOC code, OOH page, and annual OEWS wage/employment estimate.
practice_differences.growth_engineer_and_ai_engineer: Neither has a BLS SOC code or OOH/OEWS entry; both are defined only by industry practitioner sources and tracked only indirectly via job-board volume.

practice_differences.description: A software engineer embedded within a Growth/Marketing team; builds A/B-testing infrastructure, funnel/cohort instrumentation, feature-flag systems, lifecycle triggers and attribution — optimizes business metrics directly rather than performing inference or general-purpose prediction.
